summary: John B. Cobb Jr. is a philosopher and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago. He held professorships at Claremont School of Theology and Claremont Graduate University (attested 1989) and founded the Center for Process Studies.

John Borthwick Gilchrist worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Royal High School and the University of Edinburgh. He served as principal of Fort William College (1800-1804) and later became the first Professor of Hindustani at University College London (~1828-1831).
John Brockington is an Indologist who spent his career at the University of Edinburgh, where he served as Senior Lecturer in Sanskrit (attested 1987) and Professor of Sanskrit (attested 1998-2003).

John Brough was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Edinburgh under Arthur Berriedale Keith and Cambridge under Harold Walter Bailey. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at the University of London (1948-1967) and Professor at the University of Cambridge (1967-1984).
John Buescher is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his doctoral dissertation at the University of Virginia in 1982 and served as Director at Voice of America (attested 2001).

John Burnet was a scholar in philosophy who studied at the Royal High School, the University of Edinburgh, and Balliol College, Oxford. He held a post at the University of St Andrews from roughly 1892 to 1926.

John Burton-Page was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Royal College of Music and the University of Oxford. He held posts at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (~1949-1953) and SOAS University of London (~1953-1984).
John C. Huntington was a scholar of art history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He served as a professor at Ohio State University (attested 1987-1990 and 2000).

John C. Maraldo is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Japanology. He served at the University of North Florida, where he was attested in 1988 and later served as distinguished professor emeritus of philosophy (attested 2015).
John Caspar Leyden was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1790-1797). In 1808, he served as professor of Hindustani at Fort William College.

John Chadwick was a linguist and classicist who studied at Corpus Christi College, Cambridge. He worked on the Oxford Latin Dictionary (~1946-1952) and served at the University of Cambridge as a lecturer and Reader in Classics (1969-1984).

John Claude White worked in Tibetology and archaeology, having studied at Rugby School and the Royal Indian Engineering College (~1873-1876). In 1876, he became an Assistant Engineer for the Bengal Public Works Department.

John Clifford Holt is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied under Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah at the University of Chicago. He served as Professor of Religion at Bowdoin College (~1978-2019) and held the Numata Chair at Calgary (2006).

John Collinson Nesfield was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Merton College. He served as principal of Government Sanskrit College, Varanasi (1878), and held professorships at Krishnagar Government College and Presidency College, Chennai.

John Corrigan is a religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Chicago. He taught at Arizona State University (~1990-2001) before becoming a Distinguished Professor of Religion and Professor of History at Florida State University (~2001).

John Crawfurd was a historian and linguist who studied medicine at the University of Edinburgh (~1800-1803). He served as a physician for the East India Company (1803-1808) and succeeded Stamford Raffles in 1823.

John Crook was an ethologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his doctorate at Cambridge under Robert Hinde and William Homan Thorpe, studied under Sheng Yen, and taught at the University of Bristol (1977).

John D. Dunne is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy who earned his PhD at Harvard under Masatoshi Nagatomi and Malcolm David Eckel. He held posts at Emory University (~2005-2016) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1999).

John D. Smith is an Indologist and linguist. He served as a Lecturer in Sanskrit at SOAS University of London (1975) and later at the University of Cambridge (1984), where he was a Professor from 2001 to 2007.

John Daido Loori was a Buddhist practitioner and scholar who studied under Soen Nakagawa and Taizan Maezumi, and attended Rutgers University. He served as Abbot of Zen Mountain Monastery from around 1980 until 2009.
